highlights.title: Dialog target raised, Buy
highlights.text: HNB Stockbrokers raised its Dialog Axiata (DIAL.N0000) target to Rs 59.40 from Rs 55 and rates it Buy (24% upside from Rs 48, about 31% with dividends; its weekly table still shows Moderate buy at Rs 55), on a DCF at a 12.97% WACC and 5% terminal growth; it sees DPS rising from Rs 2.80 (FY26E) to Rs 3.80 (FY28E). That is about twice this site's Dialog fair value of Rs 29.05 (buy below Rs 24.69), a big disagreement.

highlights.text: The market slipped on 23 Nov: the ASPI fell 0.60% (−127.20 points) to 21,242.52 and the S&P SL20 0.48% to 6,046.17 on thin turnover of Rs 1.05bn. Foreigners were net buyers of Rs 29.94M (bought Rs 64M, sold Rs 34M), though Dialog saw about Rs 29M of foreign selling. highlights.text: The IMF board meets on 2 Dec on Sri Lanka's seventh review, which could release about $345mn. Asian markets slumped on Monday morning after last week's AI and chip sell-off (Nikkei −5.06%, KOSPI −4.07%), while US futures bounced.

research.report: Research report: 'The Potential Dividend Compounder: Rising Yield, Defensible Earnings' (HNB Stockbrokers, November 2026)
keyPoints: Consolidation (Airtel Lanka bought in 2024; three mobile operators instead of four, mobile HHI up from 3,142 in 2020 to 4,629) gives Dialog, with over 60% of mobile, pricing power and scale; EBITDA margin was 51.9% on a trailing basis vs 42.0% for regional peers.

Margin gains now come from spreading a largely fixed network cost over more revenue rather than cutting variable costs; lower depreciation (27% of revenue in FY25 to about 25% in FY27E) adds to EBIT margin.

Revenue growth slows to about 5% a year (FY25–FY28E) and is ARPU-led: mobile subscribers about +1% a year, mobile ARPU about +3% a year from FY27E, fixed broadband ARPU +2% rising to +4%, pay-TV ARPU below +2% as streaming bites. EBITDA grows about 10% a year.

Capex rises with 5G to a peak of about 21% of revenue in FY28E, then eases; free cash flow to equity stays around Rs 50bn a year, so the payout rises from about 70% to over 80% and net debt/EBITDA falls from about 0.7x to about 0.4x by FY27E.

Valuation: 10-year DCF gives Rs 59.49 a share (enterprise value Rs 598.9bn, less debt Rs 77.3bn plus cash Rs 30.1bn); cost of equity 16.0% (11.0% five-year bond yield, beta 1.0, 5.0% premium), pre-tax cost of debt 10.5%, 35:65 debt:equity, WACC 12.97%, terminal growth 5.0%. Sensitivity range Rs 55.51–63.80 (±1 point on WACC and terminal growth); peer multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, EV/sales) give higher ranges.

glance: Buy, target raised to Rs 59.40 from Rs 55: about 24% above Rs 48, about 31% with the Rs 3.25 of dividends they expect in the next 12 months.

details.title: Overview and share details
points: Sri Lanka's leading mobile, broadband and pay-TV provider; over 60% of the core mobile market after buying Airtel Lanka in 2024 for shares.
Axiata Group (Malaysia) owns about 74% and Bharti Airtel about 10%.
Market value about Rs 437bn, the largest company on the CSE; about Rs 66bn after adjusting for the free float.
Directors' and managers' net share sales were only about Rs 6.7mn over 8 years.
A new employee share plan (May 2026): 2% new shares over 10 years, about Rs 8.7bn at today's price, which they say aligns management with shareholders.
Also owns a finance company it plans to use for fintech products.

details.title: Investment thesis
points: Consolidation: mobile operators down from four to three; market concentration (HHI) up from 3,142 in 2020 to 4,629 (above 2,500 counts as highly concentrated).
EBITDA margin up 570 bps; future gains come from spreading a mostly fixed network cost over more revenue, not from cutting variable costs.
Defensive cash flows: subscription-based, demand for connectivity barely moves with the economy; little exposure to AI and data-centre spending.
Capex rises with 5G to a peak of about 21% of revenue in FY28E, then eases.
Payout to rise from about 70% (FY26E) to over 80%; dividend from Rs 2.80 (FY26E) to over Rs 4.00 within the forecast period.
Net debt / EBITDA about 0.7x now, among the lowest of regional peers, falling to about 0.4x by FY27E; dividends seen as a floor for the share price.

tables.title: Five forces in developed markets (text table) (Exhibit 5F-DM, p. 15)
points: New entrants: moderate. Low-cost resellers renting networks (US cable firms took 76% of North American net mobile additions in 1Q 2026); new networks very costly (EchoStar quit, Rakuten took 5 years to break even).
Suppliers: moderate to high. Costly spectrum (US C-band ≈$81bn), fewer vendors after Huawei/ZTE phase-out, handset makers pass on costs.
Buyers: moderate to high. Number portability makes switching easy (SK Telecom lost ≈650,000 in 2 months); Europe's GDP-adjusted ARPU €14.9 in 2024 vs €15.3 in 2015; regulators cap price rises.
Substitutes: moderate. OTT apps already took voice/SMS; satellite-to-phone (SpaceX bought $17bn of spectrum) not yet a big threat; private 5G for enterprises.
Rivalry: moderate to high. Saturated (US penetration ≈98%), Europe fragmented (44 operators vs 8 US, 4 Japan); consolidation (VodafoneThree, M1) is the fix.

tables.title: Five forces in Sri Lanka (text table) (Exhibit 5F-SL, p. 16)
points: New entrants: low. Dialog has invested over $3.45bn; only Dialog and SLT bid in the first 5G auction (Dec 2025); penetration ≈127%, so a newcomer must take customers.
Suppliers: moderate. Government controls spectrum and tariff approvals; dollar-priced equipment from few vendors; scale gives Dialog better terms.
Buyers: moderate to low. No number portability yet (delayed several times); multi-SIM use common, but 2025 tariff rises held and Dialog's ARPU rose 12%.
Substitutes: moderate. OTT apps (smartphone penetration over 70%) still use operators' data; Starlink launched July 2025, not a near-term threat; streaming pressures pay TV.
Rivalry: moderate to low. Three operators, Dialog 64%; SLT the only other 5G holder, Hutch a value brand; competition on quality, not price.
Watch: number portability, a change in SLT's ownership, Hutch entering 5G.

details.title: Revenue and margin drivers
points: Revenue growth slows to about 5% a year (FY25–FY28E), from 8% over the last five years, as one-off drivers fade.
Mobile subscribers about +1% a year; fixed broadband subscribers +2–3%.
Mobile ARPU about +7% in FY26E, then about +3% a year from FY27E; fixed broadband ARPU flat in FY26E, then +2% rising to +4%; pay-TV ARPU under +2% as streaming bites.
Over 44% of network costs are fixed: historically a 1% revenue change has moved operating profit about 2.3%.
Depreciation to fall from 27% of revenue (FY25) to about 25% (FY27E); EBITDA margin from 52.1% to about 54.3% by FY27E; EBITDA growth about 10% a year (FY25–FY28E), about 7% from FY26E.

details.title: Checks on the report
points: Their asset base grows faster than their cash capex explains. Fixed assets (p. 46) less depreciation plus cash capex (p. 47) leave about Rs 22.7bn (FY26E), Rs 19.5bn (FY27E) and Rs 16.0bn (FY28E) of extra additions each year (worked out by this site from their printed figures). Leases explain only part of it. Their FCFF deducts only the cash capex.
Previous target: p. 4 says Rs 55.00, the chart on p. 43 marks Rs 50.00.
Beta: p. 4 shows 0.9; the DCF uses 1.0; the average on their beta chart is about 0.82.
Five forces: the text says Sri Lanka scores lower on every force, but substitutes are rated moderate in both (pp. 15–17).
Depreciation's share of the FY27E EBIT margin rise: 'roughly half' in the heading, 'over 20%' in the text (p. 31).

Sign errors in the income statement (p. 45): FY21 cost of sales positive, FY23 finance cost +162, FY22 profit before and after tax positive although shareholders' profit is a Rs 33.4bn loss.

news.title: IMF board to take up Sri Lanka's seventh review on 2 Dec
news.text: Approval would release about $345mn under the $2.9bn programme, which ends in March 2027; the review includes waivers and changes to performance criteria. A committee is studying a follow-up arrangement (a funded Stand-By Arrangement or a Policy Coordination Instrument are options). Foreign debt service is about $3bn in 2027 and $3.6bn in 2028; reserves are about $7bn, and growth is projected at 4% in 2027.

news.title: Credit growth slows to 21.8% but stays high
news.text: Since May's 100bps hike, the call money rate is up 108bps, the one-year T-bill 146bps and the weekly prime lending rate 166bps, yet private credit still grows about 21.8% a year, which helped prompt last week's second hike. The Governor named personal loans, pawning and financial services as the fastest-growing areas, defended the 70% loan-to-value cap on gold loans, and said the deposit-rate cap on finance companies stays.

news.title: Central Bank to get tradeable bonds to soak up liquidity
news.text: From March 2027 the step-down coupons on the Central Bank's restructured government bonds end and they become ordinary 5% fixed-rate bonds, which it can sell at a discount to drain excess rupees from banks instead of issuing its own securities or raising reserve requirements.

news.title: Sinopec's Hambantota refinery stalls
news.text: The proposed $3.7bn, 200,000-barrel-a-day refinery has stalled after Sinopec withdrew over market access and tax relief; there is no penalty as no letter of intent was signed. Options include a joint venture with Lanka IOC, a PPP tender, and the Sapugaskanda refinery upgrade (expressions of interest shortlisted). The Energy Minister wants two more months to decide.

news.title: Construction support centre ahead of Rs 2tn development budget
news.text: The 'Builders' Gateway' centre, under the Presidential Secretariat, will help contractors and suppliers resolve tender, contract and administrative problems free of charge as the Government prepares a Rs 2tn development budget for 2027; about 95% of public project work is done by the private sector.

news.title: Minimum export prices planned for coconut charcoal and fresh nuts
news.text: The Coconut Development Authority will set minimum declared export prices rather than ban exports: fresh nuts from about $0.40 to $0.70–0.80 a nut, and a floor (not yet announced) for shell charcoal, now exported at $300–330/t while local activated carbon makers import it at about $380/t. Government approval is pending.

news.title: Tourist arrivals pass 2 million for the third year
news.text: Arrivals crossed 2 million on 20 Nov, three days later than in 2025, after a slump in March and April, so the year is still behind last year's pace despite strong growth from India. A Rs 1.5bn interim promotion drive is rolling out late: UK and Germany campaigns (Rs 100mn each) are awarded, Australia has run since August, and India, China and Russia are in final procurement.

news.title: Asia braces after AI sell-off; US futures bounce
news.text: US stock futures recovered on Monday while Asian markets fell and regional authorities prepared support after last week's sell-off in tech and chip stocks.

news.title: Middle East: new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain
news.text: Saudi Arabia intercepted a Houthi drone and missile and Bahrain reported an Iranian strike on an industrial site; Iran's foreign minister said the June Islamabad memorandum is off the table but Iran is open to a deal with the US. Tankers were hit near Oman, though oil prices have fallen for three weeks.
